findings.text: the fallback at :736-767 rebuilds the closed boundary from a contourpy marching-squares loop filtered by matplotlib.path.Path containment, and then from stored core cells, so the committed cpu-lane state renders only through the Matplotlib-contour path that separatrix-spline-extraction §4 replaced with the shared comparator; the coordinator's resume instruction was explicit that a committed state predating the schema is a recorded follow-on and that no fallback may be added, so this commit cannot land as written.

the writer still persists wall_z while _restore_units at :436 now prefers wall_z and falls back to wall_height, so the state schema carries two spellings and a freshly written state stays unreadable to the pre-rename reader; the directed repair was to restore the persisted name wall_height in both the writer and the reader.

_solved_boundary already returns the closed contour at a level that encloses the magnetic axis, and the fallback at :736-755 duplicates it with different semantics (longest line rather than largest polygon area, no validity repair), leaving two divergent implementations of one selection in the same file.

no test loads a committed docs/figures/mast-centroid-capability/*/panel-fields.npz through the panels state path, so the regression this increment exists to repair is guarded only by manually run receipts that are not a gate.

a state without coil_outlines silently yields an empty array and coil_section_count=0 in the receipt (review-final-cpu-lane-receipt.json) while the other two lanes record 938, so the cpu-lane figure omits the coil outline with no qualification a reader can see.
